entries.title: Chat says who or what it is naming
entries.body: The AI behind Chat is now asked to introduce any person, work, study or term it brings in, in a few words on who or what it is and why it matters here. That makes it more likely a name arrives with enough background to follow, including when you ask what others have said about the piece.

entries.title: More web pages show their publication date
entries.body: When a web page does not label its publication date in the way the app usually reads, the app now looks for a date written just under the title, and failing that one in the page's address, and shows it at the top of the article. This applies to articles added or processed again from now on.

entries.title: Untitled contents lists near the opening fold away
entries.body: When an article opens with a contents list that has no heading, the app can now recognise it by its links to at least three of the article's later headings, and fold it away like other contents lists. Lists such as Key points, which preview the headings, stay visible. This applies to articles added or processed again from now on.

entries.title: The Help question box grows as you type
entries.body: On the Help page, when signed in, the box for your question starts at two lines and grows and shrinks with what you write, with no scroll bar inside it. Empty boxes in the quiz, the Feedback form and the page for adding an article also keep their usual size instead of stretching to fit their grey hint text.

entries.title: arXiv titles keep their spaces and opening words
entries.body: Some arXiv papers whose title runs over two lines were saved with words glued together, such as "AGENTS.md:Are", or lost the part of the title before a colon. The line break is now read as a space and the title kept whole. This applies to papers added or processed again from now on.

entries.title: Linking claims to passages no longer fails needlessly
entries.body: The extra that links an article's claims to the passages behind them could fail when every link it found was to a neighbouring paragraph, and the message made it look as if adding the article had failed. It finishes with no links in that case. If an extra does fail, the card says the article itself is unchanged.
